edge_thesis: I claim no information edge, so I am harvesting structural premia in the cheapest-cost classes rather than predicting news. The picks are long equity drift (SPY), long term premium as an equity-shock hedge (IEF), and long trend persistence in gold (GLD), with a low-volatility balanced fund as ballast. On the other side are hedgers paying for downside insurance, short-horizon mean-reversion traders fading trends, and price-insensitive rebalancers. Each stop is at least roughly one daily range from entry, and tp and sl sit far enough apart that a single bar should rarely touch both. All tp/sl levels are anchored to my reference prices (SPY 690.00, IEF 96.00, GLD 460.00); the intended percent distances from fill are in each why field.

picks.why: Equity drift with a tight bracket: tp +1.1% / sl -0.9% from fill, about 1.2R on a win, and the 6.71bp cost is only ~0.07R.
Duration carry that tends to rally when equities sell off, offsetting SPY drawdown: tp +0.68% / sl -0.57% from fill.
Trend persistence backed by central-bank buying; wider bracket for higher volatility: tp +2.0% / sl -1.6% from fill.
Roughly 35/65 stock/bond balanced fund with zero cost and low drawdown, the single long-term NAV pick, scored on USD only.
